definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 splits 'character' into four senses (4.26 a code value of a coded character set, 4.27 a graphic character in a screen item, 4.28 a COBOL character, 4.29 a single code value in storage); 2023 drops those entries but keeps each sense under its own term (§2023:3.7 alphanumeric character, national character, §2023:3.93 graphic character, §2023:3.37 COBOL character repertoire), so the drop is of a heading, not of a meaning. 'The character ... that has the highest ordinal position' is a member of the coded character set (4.26) placed by the collating sequence, the 2023 alphanumeric/national character; confirmed now at --std 2002 and 2023 alike: ORD(HIGH-VALUE)=65536 and HIGH-VALUE = CHAR(65536) (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out-answer/probes-a-14/rw_space.cob (rw_space-2002.txt, rw_space-2023.txt)).
